title: Slim SDK artifacts, align transport adapters, and formalize API deprecation runway
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Overview: Reduce SDK artifact sizes, remove legacy API parameters that were kept for backwards compatibility, and converge transport adapter behavior across Python/JS/Go. This ticket covers inventory, version bumps, build changes, migration docs, and a staged rollout to avoid breaking production customers.

Background: Over several releases SDK packages accumulated optional extras, polyfills, and compatibility shims that increased wheel/npm tarball sizes and complicated runtime transport behavior (XHR/fetch/Node net, Go http.Client variants). A number of legacy request fields (e.g., `client_meta`, `x_legacy_retry`, `legacy_token`, and old `response_format` enums) were marked deprecated but not removed or given a formal migration path. We need a single coordinated effort to shrink client artifacts, standardize transport semantics and provide a clear deprecation runway so downstream systems can upgrade predictably.
acceptance_criteria: Published Python wheel size reduced by >= 25% (strip optional extras, remove vendorized deps)
Node package tarball reduced by >= 20% via ESM/CJS split and conditional exports
Go module builds remove duplicated vendored files and cut binary size of common examples by >= 15%
Transport adapters documented with canonical behavior matrix and compatibility tests added across Node/Py/Go
All deprecated API fields listed in migration guide with recommended replacements and sample code
Automated canary rollout completed with no customer-facing errors in first 48h; rollback plan verified
plan:
1) Inventory: run script across all SDK repos to enumerate direct and transitive deps, optional 'extras', and any vendorized packages; surface files contributing most to artifact size.
2) Define transport contract: agree on behavior for timeouts, retry semantics, headers propagation, and streaming across Python/Node/Go. Create `TRANSPORT_CONTRACT.md`.
3) Version bumps: pin target minor/major versions for core infra deps (httpx, node-fetch -> undici, protobuf/flatbuffers where used) and schedule coordinated minor releases so we don't create cascading breakages.
4) Build changes: adopt PEP 517 wheel-build isolation, split Node build into ESM and CJS outputs with conditional exports, enable minification where safe, and remove source maps from production packages where they inflate size. For Go, remove leftover examples and avoid embedding test data in the module.
5) Deprecation cleanup: remove runtime shims for deprecated fields, but keep graceful parsing for one release with warnings emitted; provide migration snippets for each language.
6) Tests: add cross-language end-to-end tests exercising transport edge cases (chunked streaming, timeouts, header case preservation).
7) Docs and SDK changelogs: update release notes and add explicit migration guide and FAQ.
8) Rollout: publish canary channels (alpha/beta tags), monitor errors and telemetry; if safe, cut GA releases and announce removal date for deprecated fields in docs and API changelog.
rollout:
Phase A (canary): publish alpha builds to internal CI and to a small set of partner orgs (2–3 teams) for 7 days.
Phase B (wider beta): publish beta to public registries with clear 'beta' tags, enable telemetry gates and monitor for 14 days.
Phase C (GA): publish stable with migration notes and update SDK Console migration banner.
Rollback: each published package must have an immediate rollback tag and a back-compat shim branch we can re-release within 24h.
